verification.sourceNote: ClaimDesk generic guidance for comparing reported circumstances with the damage seen in photos. Each finding is a neutral point for the engineer to consider, never a conclusion about the claim or the people involved. Not a substitute for the engineer's own inspection.

rules.message: The reported impact was to the {direction}, but the damage recorded is on the other side of the vehicle ({zones}). For the engineer to consider: the side may have been described from a different viewpoint (nearside and offside are easily confused), or the photos may show a different area.

Damage is recorded at {zones}, away from the reported {direction} impact. For the engineer to consider whether it relates to this incident, for example a secondary impact, earlier damage or circumstances not yet described.
No damage is recorded at the reported area of impact ({area}) in the photos assessed. For the engineer to consider: the damage may be light, hidden behind a cover, or not shown clearly in the photos.
The photos supplied do not appear to show the reported area of impact ({area}). Further photos of that area would help the engineer confirm the damage.

Heavy damage is recorded ({zones}) and the reported speed is {speed} mph. For the engineer to consider whether the damage fits the reported speed; speeds are often hard for those involved to judge, and the other vehicle's speed and mass also matter.

The reported speed is {speed} mph but only light damage is recorded in the photos. For the engineer to consider: energy-absorbing parts can hide damage behind an intact cover, so the hidden-damage checks may be worthwhile.

Airbag deployment is indicated but the visible damage is light. For the engineer to consider: deployment depends on deceleration rather than visible damage, and damage may be behind the bumper cover or underneath the vehicle.
Airbag deployment is reported but is not visible in the photos assessed. Photos of the interior would help the engineer confirm which airbags and pretensioners deployed.
The photos appear to show a deployed airbag or pretensioner although the report says none deployed. For the engineer to consider and confirm with the driver.

Some recorded damage ({zones}) shows signs that it may predate this incident, such as corrosion, dirt or weathering in the damaged area. For the engineer to consider whether it relates to this incident; any earlier damage is listed separately and not claimed.
{count} photo(s) have quality issues that limit what can be seen ({photos}). Clearer photos would improve the assessment.
